subject: humanities
passage: The Padshahnama, an official chronicle of the first decade of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan's reign, survives in its finest form in a manuscript now kept at Windsor Castle in England, where it arrived in 1799 as a gift to King George III from the ruler of Awadh. Its forty-four paintings record court ceremonies, sieges, and processions with hundreds of figures whose faces are individual enough to be portraits. Several of the paintings bear the names of the artists who made them, and specialists have used these signed pages to recognize the same ______ hands in the unsigned ones, matching the handling of textiles, horses, and faces.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The hands belong to the "artists" who signed several paintings, plural, so the blank needs a plural possessive. A plural noun ending in s forms its possessive with an apostrophe alone: "painters'."
explanation.A: Incorrect. A plural noun ending in s takes only an apostrophe to show possession; "painters's" is not standard.
explanation.B: Correct. "Painters'" is the plural possessive, showing that the hands belong to the several painters who signed the pages.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Painters" is a plain plural with no apostrophe, so it does not show that the hands belong to them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Painter's" is the possessive of a single painter, but the text refers to "the artists who made them," plural.
